privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.scope: This policy covers Kotsu at {site}. Kotsu is open source, so anyone can run a copy: a copy at another address is run by its owner, and their rules apply there.

operator.title: Who runs Kotsu
operator.text: Kotsu is run by {name}, a private individual responsible for your data here (the controller, in GDPR terms). Write to <contact>{email}</contact> with any question or request about it.

data.title: What Kotsu keeps
data.account: Your account: your email address and name. If you continue with Google, also your profile picture, your Google account ID and the sign-in tokens Google issues. Kotsu asks Google for nothing more, so those tokens can't open your mail, files or anything else in your Google account.
data.content: What you make: your shelves, docs, cards, sheets, events and practice history, and your settings, such as the language, theme and time zone.
data.signIn: Sign-in records: your sessions, with the IP address and browser of each sign-in; your passkeys (a public key and a device name: your fingerprint or face never leaves your device); one-time sign-in codes; counts of requests from each IP address and of codes sent to each email address.
data.none: No analytics, no ads, no tracking. Kotsu never sells your data.

use.title: What for
use.purposes: Only to run Kotsu: to sign you in, to keep and show what you make, to email you sign-in codes, and to stop people guessing codes or breaking into accounts.
use.basis: Under the GDPR, this rests on our agreement: Kotsu can't do what you use it for without this data (Article 6(1)(b)). Sign-in records also serve Kotsu's legitimate interest in keeping accounts safe (Article 6(1)(f)).

sharing.title: Who else gets it
sharing.intro: Only the services Kotsu runs on, each for its own part:
sharing.resend: Resend delivers the sign-in emails, so it sees your email address and the code;
sharing.google: Google, only if you continue with Google: it tells Kotsu who you are.
sharing.abroad: These are US companies, so your data may be processed in the United States, under their data protection terms. Nobody else gets your data unless the law requires it.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.intro: Kotsu sets only the cookies it needs to work:
cookies.signIn: sign-in keeps you signed in for 7 days and renews while you use Kotsu; a few more last minutes while you sign in with Google or a passkey;
cookies.choices: your choices (the theme, the language, whether the sidebar is open and whether you've answered the passkey offer) last a year.
cookies.none: No advertising or tracking cookies, and none from other sites.

retention.title: How long
retention.account: Your account and what you make: until you delete your account.
retention.signIn: A sign-in code works for 5 minutes, a session for 7 days without a visit, a count of requests from an IP address is kept for a minute, and a count of codes sent to an email address for 15 minutes. Once expired, they're deleted automatically. Your sessions, passkeys and Google link are deleted with your account.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can ask to see your data, get a copy, correct it or delete it, and object to or limit how Kotsu uses it. Write to <contact>{email}</contact> from the address you sign in with; you'll get an answer within a month.
rights.complaint: You can also complain to the data protection authority of the country you live in.

deletion.title: Deleting your account
deletion.text: Settings will get a button for it. Until then, write to <contact>{email}</contact> from the address you sign in with, and your account and everything in it will be deleted within a month.

changes.text: When this policy changes, so does the date at the top.
